There is a quiet hour just before sunrise when the world seems to hesitate. Streetlights still burn, but their glow grows tired, as if they know they are no longer needed. In that hour, the air feels unwritten. No horns, no hurried footsteps, only a hush that invites thought.

I have always loved this hour, not because it is beautiful in an obvious way, but because it asks nothing of me. It does not demand productivity or optimism. It simply exists, and in its stillness I can hear the softer parts of myself. Dreams linger at the edge of memory, fragile and strange, like messages from a kinder mind.

Sometimes I wonder whether we are most honest in moments like these, before we put on our daytime faces. The night leaves traces on us: worries we tried to solve, hopes we were afraid to name. Dawn does not erase them. Instead, it folds them into light, making them easier to carry.

A bird begins. Then another. The sky shifts from gray to pale gold, and ordinary things return: windows, rooftops, the shape of trees. Soon the streets will fill with purpose. But for now, there is only this pause, this breath between what was and what will be.

I think that is why I keep waking early. Not to see the sun rise, but to remember that I, too, can begin again. Perhaps every morning offers a quiet invitation to become less afraid of our own becoming, however slowly, always.
